title: Trump's 'Covfefe' Tweet Stayed Online for Nearly Six Hours
description_short: Trump tweeted “Despite the constant negative press covfefe” at 12:06 a.m. on May 31, 2017, deleted it before 6 a.m., then asked who could figure out “covfefe.”
description_medium: At 12:06 a.m. Eastern on May 31, 2017, Donald Trump tweeted, “Despite the constant negative press covfefe.” The Washington Post reported that he deleted the unfinished post at 5:48 a.m. and then asked, “Who can figure out the true meaning of ‘covfefe’ ??? Enjoy!” The word became a Twitter trend as users posted jokes and guesses.
description_long: At 12:06 a.m. Eastern on May 31, 2017, Donald Trump posted, “Despite the constant negative press covfefe.” The Washington Post described the message as a sentence fragment that ended abruptly. It remained on Twitter until 5:48 a.m., when Trump deleted it. While it was online, users guessed at the unfinished word and made jokes. The newspaper said “covfefe” became a trend, producing the “#covfefe” and “Rosebud” trending topics and a Twitter Moment. It also recounted users’ wordplay, including one person joking about ordering a grande “covfefe,” while some commenters defended the post as a possible human error. The article noted that Merriam-Webster’s site suggested words such as “coffee,” “coven,” and “cover” when searching for “covfefe.” After deleting the original, Trump posted: “Who can figure out the true meaning of ‘covfefe’ ??? Enjoy!” The follow-up invited speculation but did not explain the original wording. The reporting leaves Trump’s intended word or meaning unresolved.

limitations: The article does not establish what Trump intended to write or the meaning of covfefe.
